sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Cryo-EM structure of the BRIL-PTGDR2 complex was determined, confirming proper folding and membrane insertion; surface expression of the HA-mDP2 ortholog confirmed by immunofluorescence (anti-HA and MAb-1D8 staining). No ligand-binding or signalling functional assay reported for the tagged constructs.
sites.rationale: PTGDR2 has a 33-residue extracellular N-terminal domain (topology landmarks 1–33) followed by TM1 at residue 34, giving 33 residues of clearance from the TM boundary — well above the ≥3-residue minimum. The N-terminus is the only extracellular terminus of this 7-TM GPCR, so a tag reported at 'the N-terminus' of the full-length receptor can only sit at insert_after_residue=0 (prepend before M1). Python confirmed residue 1 = M and residue 34 = A. L3 and L4 both directly report BRIL at the N-terminus of human PTGDR2 in full-length membrane-anchored constructs used for structural studies; L5/L6 independently confirm surface display of an N-terminal tag on the mouse ortholog. PMC11665870 (L3) reports a BRIL tag introduced at the N-terminus of full-length, membrane-anchored human PTGDR2 (DP2), with C-terminal residues 349–395 truncated, for cryo-EM structural studies. A second construct in the same paper (L4) adds a prolactin signal peptide before the BRIL and an LgBiT at the C-terminus. No residue number is named for the junction; PTGDR2 has exactly one extracellular terminus (residues 1–33), so the tag prepends before residue 1 (M). Indirect corroboration from PMC5386288 (L5/L6): an HA-tagged mouse DP2 ortholog showed plasma-membrane surface staining by immunofluorescence identical to anti-HA staining, confirming extracellular display of an N-terminal tag on this receptor.

sources.claim: First, a BRIL tag was introduced at the N terminus of DP2, and the C-terminal residues 349 to 395 were truncated ( 24 , 25 ) ( SI Appendix , Fig.

literature_notes: L1 and L2 (PMC6223628) report eT4L/mT4L domain insertions into ICL3 of CRTH2 (=PTGDR2) between residues R236 and R238. The topology landmarks place ICL3 at residues 232–247 (intracellular); these insertions are cytoplasmic and do not qualify as surface tag sites — recorded in other_positions. L4 also reports an LgBiT fused to the C-terminus of PTGDR2; the C-terminus (residues 309–395) is intracellular per the topology landmarks and is likewise recorded in other_positions. No ledger line grounds a tag in any of the three extracellular loops (ECL1 90–106, ECL2 169–210, ECL3 270–288), so no internal sites are proposed. L5/L6 describe HA-tagged mouse DP2 with confirmed surface staining but name no residue and no loop; since the N-terminus is the only extracellular terminus, this collapses onto the same topology_derived prepend already grounded by L3.
